best_feature: Three-scenario unit economics with LTV/CAC and the 6-hours-a-week capacity math show concretely why it cannot earn a living, with go/kill lines on each experiment.
weakness: Very long and table-heavy, with many tagged guesses and three experiments plus three escape routes, which would overwhelm an easily overwhelmed reader.

best_feature: Plain-language verdict (no full launch, yes to a cheap test) with a step-by-step validation plan that includes a producer-partner idea and explicit go/rethink/stop criteria.
weakness: Still fairly long, with several risk sections and variations before the first step, and its unit economics are only loose ranges.

best_feature: Founder-capacity and break-even reasoning (about 280 subscribers for 1M ARR, 2-3 subscribers at 6 hours) plus a concrete single thing to do this week.
weakness: Verdict wavers between 'don't launch yet' and 'Pivot it', and the long skill-template structure (scorecard, five questions, memory-sourced company links) buries the answer.

best_feature: A copy-paste text to the three friends asking for a EUR 20 prepayment within 30 minutes, with a numeric pass/stop threshold and a dated deadline.
weakness: Jargon-heavy (E1, adjusted 2.0, idea-to-plan) and repeats itself in two verdict blocks with differing labels, and the economics are thin.

best_feature: Clear 'not a launch, yes to a small test' verdict with a three-step plan and explicit go/rethink/stop thresholds, while dismantling each piece of the user's evidence.
weakness: Still fairly long with many sections and a first step (30+ conversations, landing page) that is more than one tiny action.

best_feature: Scenario table with contribution, LTV/CAC and the finding that 6 hours supports only ~8 subscribers at about EUR 10/hour exposes the real economics.
weakness: Very long, dense and tag-heavy with many tables and numbers (some guesses), which would overwhelm an ADHD reader and buries the single first step.

best_feature: A 30-minute first step (text three friends asking for a EUR 20 prepay plus three colleagues each) with a 14-day pass/stop criterion.
weakness: Framework jargon (scores, E1, D 2.0, tool names) and two overlapping blocks make it cluttered, and the economics are thin.

best_feature: Fatal-questions structure, including the 1M ARR sanity check and the idea to sell to hospitals or partner with a licensed kitchen.
weakness: Long, with a scorecard, competitor list and three experiments plus a 'pivot' verdict that is less crisp, and it makes its own assumptions (10 meals for EUR 69) that muddy the economics.

best_feature: Quantified scenario economics (break-even, ceiling, about EUR 7/hour pessimistic case) with a 30-day gated test and explicit kill criteria.
weakness: Very long and dense, with many invented scenario numbers and tables that would overwhelm an easily overwhelmed reader and leaks process meta-talk (dossier, model script).

best_feature: Gives a concrete 30-minute first action and a falsifiable test with pass and stop thresholds, plus the sharp pre-mortem about stale paid status.
weakness: Two pasted evaluations with conflicting verdicts (Start vs Fix first) and internal jargon (E3, Priority A, adj. 3.5) make it confusing and hard to act on.

best_feature: Clear Pivot verdict with a cheap sequenced start (audit own data, then convert the four deposits to a price) and hard caps on time, spend and a 90-day bar.
weakness: Long with a scorecard framework and some leaked tooling references (skill founder files), more than a person with ADHD needs.

best_feature: Sharp critique of the evidence (why only 2 of 4 improved, noisy small-n percentages) plus practical build and deliverability pitfalls and a budget breakdown.
weakness: A 12-week plan with many steps and no single cheap first step with stop criterion, and gates only at week 12.

best_feature: Clear 'time-boxed experiment, not yet a business' verdict with a week-by-week plan, a budget split and explicit continue/stop gates, plus the sharp point that 2 of 4 non-improvers must be understood first.
weakness: Long, with a 12-week plan and many sub-steps, which could overwhelm an easily overloaded reader and gives no single obvious first action.

best_feature: Concrete unit economics (break-even users, users needed for EUR 1,000/month, EUR 7/hour pessimistic case) and a 30-day plan with explicit pass/kill thresholds.
weakness: Dense scenario tables built on guessed growth and churn rates, plus meta-talk about skipped dossier/model files, make it heavy and partly speculative.

best_feature: Short and decisive: a 30-minute first step, a specific test (4 of 10 strangers pay EUR 9/month) with pass and stop thresholds, and a good pre-mortem about stale paid-status causing wrong reminders.
weakness: Jargon-laden scoring (Priority A, E3, adjusted 3.5) and two stacked verdicts ('Start' and 'Fix first') read as inconsistent and are less natural for the user.

best_feature: Three cheap experiments with success thresholds (audit own data, convert deposits to price, test strangers) and a clear 'do this week' first step.
weakness: Long, with a scorecard and a 'Pivot it' verdict (18/35, built on made-up scoring) that sits oddly with the 'don't kill it' advice, plus leaked references to skill files.

best_feature: Clean, plain-language ranking (start #4, test course second, drop sensor and marketplace, park YouTube) with a week-by-week table and a cheap pre-sale test with a clear commit threshold.
weakness: Price ranges and revenue outlook are loosely hedged guesses and the course stop criterion is not tied to a firm date or the retainer step.

best_feature: Gives an immediate 30-minute first step plus dated tests with explicit pass/stop criteria, and labels assumptions and estimates as unverified.
weakness: Dense jargon-filled format (Adj. score, E-levels, Prio) and renumbered ideas that do not match the user's list, which is confusing and shallow on why each idea fails.

best_feature: Most thorough analysis of each idea's economics, competition and fit with 6 h/week, with explicit unverified flags and a realistic income cap for the freelance service.
weakness: Very long, with scorecard, three simultaneous experiments, many competitor links and a multi-part plan that would overwhelm an easily overwhelmed reader.

best_feature: Explicit pass/fail experiments with thresholds (E1-E3) and heavily flagged unverified claims, plus a clear start/pivot/kill verdict per idea.
weakness: At about 1800 words with a 7-dimension scorecard, three experiments and many links, it is far too long and heavy for an easily overwhelmed person.

best_feature: Compact, dated tests with explicit pass and stop criteria and a pre-mortem, with every estimate labelled assumed or unverified.
weakness: Jargon-dense and confusingly renumbers the ideas in the table (report service as #1, course as #2), and has skill-chain residue, so the ranking is harder to read than it should be.

best_feature: Clear sequence of start #4, test #1 on the back of it, drop #2 and #3, park #5, with a simple weekly plan fitted to 6 hours and a retainer-cap risk note.
weakness: Gives no explicit stop criterion for the freelance start, and states the price ranges and the YouTube Partner Programme thresholds with only light uncertainty flags.

best_feature: A concrete 14-day deposit test with explicit pass/stop thresholds plus a worked capacity calculation (about 4 h/week gives roughly 3-4 subscribers).
weakness: Two stacked reports full of internal jargon (Recycle, Priority C, E1, x0.85 scores) with a muddled verdict that would confuse and overwhelm a non-expert.

best_feature: Plain-language verdict that dissects each piece of evidence (40% stat, market size, friends' praise) and covers real risks like German food law, thin economics, the producer-partner route and go/rethink/stop criteria.
weakness: Long, with a multi-step 4-6 week plan rather than one tiny first action, and it adds some unsourced estimates (salary range, cost figures) that could overwhelm and are only lightly flagged.

best_feature: Extremely cheap first step (text three friends today asking for a EUR 20 prepay and 3 colleague referrals) with a dated test and a stop threshold.
weakness: Dense scoring jargon, duplicated two-part structure, and thinner economics (margin left unknown, odd dry-run criteria) make it hard to follow and less insightful.

best_feature: Cautious, clear verdict (test with 20 strangers before building) with a concrete 30-minute first step, pass/stop thresholds, a EUR 150 spend cap, and honest handling of n=4 and the self-run confound.
weakness: Two overlapping verdicts in one answer, packed with internal jargon (E3, Priority B, adjusted score, E0) and dense one-line fragments that would overwhelm and confuse a non-expert.

best_feature: Plain-language verdict with a balanced read of the evidence (no control, half did not improve, EUR 20 is not subscription intent), real competition and build risks (deliverability, OAuth, GDPR), a budget breakdown, and explicit continue/stop gates.
weakness: Long, with a 12-week plan, budget lines and many tasks, and no single cheapest first step with a stop criterion, which is heavy for someone easily overwhelmed.

best_feature: Cheap first step (email the 4 users for invoice and paid dates to verify the drop and ask for a monthly commitment) plus a sharp pre-mortem about stale paid status causing wrong reminders.
weakness: Rates the idea Priority A with Demand 4 on only four friendly deposits, which overstates weak evidence, and it gives two conflicting verdicts (Start vs Fix first) in jargon-heavy, duplicated text.

best_feature: Concrete 30-minute first step (reply to the agency, propose a fixed-price pilot) plus a pass/stop test with dates, and prices are explicitly labeled as assumptions.
weakness: Jargon-heavy (Adj. score, E2, Prio) with a table covering only three ideas, so the full ranking of all five and the drop/park distinction is muddled for a non-expert.

best_feature: Names one 30-minute action, a 14-day paid-pilot test with explicit pass and stop thresholds, a realistic capacity ceiling of 2-3 clients at about 4 hours a week, and a clear drop of the sensor with a cheap pivot.
weakness: Still uses scoring jargon and a dense format, and lists the course as both parked and a second table item, which is slightly inconsistent.

best_feature: Plain-language ranking with a clear start, second step, drop and park for every idea, including sound reasons such as the marketplace cold start and CE certification for hardware, plus a week-by-week plan.
weakness: Long, with no explicit stop criterion for the main idea and with specific price ranges and a YouTube monetization threshold stated without verification, which could overwhelm an easily overwhelmed reader.
